title: The whole morning
hookLine: assemble your morning in under ten minutes
tomorrow: a new law bans prayer. why does Daniel open his windows?

cards: A morning-routine video can run twenty steps and still leave you late. Sikh tradition remembers a morning with fewer steps and far more at stake.
The young Nanak, working as a storekeeper in Sultanpur, went down to the river Bein at dawn to bathe. That morning he went into the water and didn't come out. His friends searched the banks.
Tradition says that days later he came back, and the first thing he said was: there is no Hindu, there is no Muslim.

teach.b: The janamsakhis, the old life stories of Guru Nanak, say that in the river he was taken into God's presence and given a calling: to praise the Name and teach others to do the same.
Sikhs honor him as their first Guru, and his own hymn puts that dawn at the center of the day.

teach.h: AMRIT VELA: THE HOURS BEFORE DAWN.
teach.b: In Japji Sahib, the hymn that opens the Guru Granth Sahib, he says, in paraphrase: in the ambrosial hours before dawn, meditate on the True Name and on God's greatness. That's the teaching, and it shapes the Sikh morning.
Amrit vela, the ambrosial hours, is the time to rise, bathe and remember the Name, and the Sikh code of conduct, the Rehat Maryada, asks Sikhs to recite Japji Sahib among their morning prayers.
Notice what makes it a whole morning.

teach.h: A FEW FIXED PIECES, ONE CENTER.
teach.b: Not twenty steps, but a few fixed ones, in the same order, around one center: water, then the Name, then the words. Nanak's river story fits that center: in the janamsakhis' telling, his calling came at a dawn bath.

On your own path, here is the week's work, assembled the same way: the first minute, three breaths before the phone, your morning line, one intention, a stretch, one thanks, a quick preview of who you'll meet.
Under ten minutes. One center you come back to.

how: The Sikh Rehat Maryada asks Sikhs to rise in the amrit vela, bathe, meditate on the Name and recite Japji Sahib and the other morning prayers of the nitnem.

o: every habit you've ever tried, done all at once
a few practices in a fixed order, around one center
whatever you happen to do before work starts

p: where Nanak went in at dawn
the hymn that opens the Guru Granth Sahib

s: a real morning practice needs many steps and a lot of time
the Sikh morning keeps a few fixed pieces around one center: rise, bathe, the Name.
Japji Sahib speaks of meditating on the True Name in the hours before dawn
Nanak came out of the river saying people should leave the world behind

games.q: your neighbor's morning routine changes every week: a new app, new steps, a new order. what would the Sikh morning suggest?
o: a few fixed pieces in the same order, around one center.
a brand-new routine each week, so it never goes stale.
more steps each week, so the morning feels complete.
games.why: amrit vela keeps the same order every day: rise, bathe, remember the Name. the center holds the rest.

practice: Open your notebook and write your whole morning as a short list, in order, the way a Sikh morning keeps its order. Keep only the pieces you'll truly do, and check that the list fits inside ten minutes.
Then read it once, slowly, as if it were already tomorrow morning.

wordCard.voice: The whole morning: a few practices in a fixed order, around one center. For Sikhs, amrit vela: rise, bathe, remember the Name.

carryVoice: Your line: my morning. A few pieces, one center, kept in order. A fresh week has begun.
